plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Long after summer gardens have faded, bare corms push up goblets of soft lilac-pink, crocus-like flowers with no leaves at all. They look like a carpet of delicate chalices spread across damp meadows and borders. The white form 'Album' glows in the low autumn light.
plants.location: Temperate Europe, and widely grown in gardens in cooler parts of North America such as the Midwest and Northeast United States
plants.funFact: Autumn crocus is nicknamed 'naked ladies' because the flowers appear without foliage. The leaves emerge the following spring and then die back before the flowers return. Every part of the plant is toxic, and it is the natural source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and in plant breeding.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novi-belgii
plants.description: A cloud of starry, daisy-like flowers with golden-yellow centers and rays of rich violet to lavender-blue. Its tall, bushy clumps light up late-season borders and roadsides. Bees and butterflies crowd onto the flowers as other nectar sources run out.
plants.bloomingSeason: August through October, peaking in early autumn
plants.location: Eastern North America, from the Atlantic coast and Canadian Maritimes south through the Appalachians. It is also a garden favorite across Europe.
plants.funFact: Asters take their name from the Greek word for 'star'. In Britain, they are called Michaelmas daisies because they bloom around Michaelmas, the feast of St. Michael on September 29, which is almost exactly your date.
